fakesni.title: Fake SNI

warning.title: Read this before turning Fake SNI on
warning.p1: Fake SNI decrypts HTTPS for domains with an sni= rule, then opens a new connection to the server with a fake domain name so your ISP cannot see which site you visit.
warning.p2: Meanwhile Ghostline sees the decrypted content of those domains. It stays in RAM only and is never stored or logged.
warning.p3: Apps that pin certificates (some banking apps, native apps) will fail for those domains.
warning.p4: Do not use it for banking or important accounts.
warning.p5: The Ghostline root certificate installed in Windows can sign only the domains in your rules and is removed when you disconnect.
warning.p6: It applies only to browsers on this PC going through Ghostline's proxy.

fakesni.caNone: no session CA (Fake SNI is not running)
fakesni.firefox: Firefox: if it reports a certificate error, set security.enterprise_roots.enabled in about:config.
fakesni.banner: Fake SNI is on — Ghostline is decrypting HTTPS for {{count}} domains

lookup.name: domain
lookup.placeholder: e.g. youtube.com, or an IP for PTR
lookup.addSourceHint: server URL/stamp, or a plain DNS IP
lookup.ispNote: The ISP DNS source sends an unencrypted query: your ISP sees the domain you look up. Use it only to compare when diagnosing.

poisoned.title: DNS is poisoned
poisoned.body: At least one source answered a private IP, or said the domain does not exist while another source has addresses. That is how ISPs block with DNS.

differs.title: Answers differ
differs.body: The sources answered different addresses. CDNs answer by location, so this is not necessarily blocking.

match.title: Answers match
match.body: The sources answered the same addresses (or the same CDN).

failed.title: No source answered
failed.body: Every source failed or timed out. Check the network.

lookup.busy: Looking up {{name}} through {{count}} sources… (at most 5 seconds each)

stamp.notUsable: Ghostline does not use this type

scanner.capped: Scanned {{max}} priority servers and skipped {{skipped}}. Raise "max servers per scan" in the options, or narrow the filter (protocol, tags).
scanner.maxServersNote: 50–2000. More servers take longer: 500 take about 1–2 minutes, 2000 about 6–8; a scan stops after at most 10 minutes.
